limits: The 32-replication aggregate log exposes one replication. The 32 explicit seeds give separately observed runs, not the aggregate run's hidden replication counts.
The explicit-seed mean count differs from the aggregate's implied mean; they are different random-stream experiments and are not forced to agree.
No zero-count seed occurred (minimum one), so the native zero-count branch is unobserved even though the frozen acceptance specified how to evaluate it.

Count precision uses 32 per-seed observations; timing precision uses one mean per nonzero-count seed. The pooled event mean is descriptive only because starts within a seed are not independent sampling units.
The nominal Student-t intervals describe this fixed convenience matrix conditional on assumptions; they do not establish Poisson or uniform laws or independent streams.
Report-bin checks use event-log times at printed precision; high-count capacity, other distributions, periods, GUI visual behavior and cross-engine equivalence remain untested.
